Now I can compare quantities against receipts.

**Ledger:**
- Earlier invoice 00874/KPI/2026 (2026-09-12, PO-2026-0208, total 11497602) — same total as this invoice.

**Receipts:** Two GRs (A: 2026-09-10, B: 2026-09-19), each 17 / 7 / 11. PO ordered 34 / 14 / 22. So total received = 34 / 14 / 22 (fully received).

**This invoice lines:** 17 / 7 / 11 — exactly one GR's worth.

**Key question:** what did invoice 00874 bill? Its total equals this invoice's total (11497602), and this invoice's line quantities (17/7/11) sum exactly to that total (subtotal 10358200 + tax 10% = 11394020... let me check).

Let me verify the arithmetic: 7469800 + 1821400 + 1067000 = 10358200. Tax 10% = 1035820. But invoice shows tax 1139402 (which is 11%). That's odd, but it's not one of the listed issues. Total 10358200 + 1139402 = 11497602.

So invoice 00874 with identical total 11497602 must have billed the same 17/7/11. If that earlier invoice (2026-09-12) was already paid and billed 17/7/11, and it preceded GR-B (dated 2026-09-19) — it could only cover GR-A.

Total invoiced if this is billed too: 34/7×2/11×2 vs received 34/14/22. That **fits within** receipt — 17+17=34 ≤ 34, 7+7=14 ≤ 14, 11+11=22 ≤ 22. And there is a goods receipt (GR-2026-0208B) for that second delivery, dated 2026-09-19 = invoice date. So this is a **separate_delivery**, not a resubmission.

Let me confirm there is no contract price/terms issue — but the only issue is possible_duplicate. The contract check returned empty. I have enough.
